subject: Help plotting original values, unstandardize predictions

messages.author: e5841ce9d01eda50
messages.subject: Help plotting original values, unstandardize predictions
parts:
Hi everyone,

I ran my model with standardized values (z-transformation), however I would now like to plot my predictions on the original scale. Does anyone have any suggestions on how to do this??

I didn't have much luck finding code much discussion or suggestions about this. And the couple codes I did find I didn't have any luck getting to work.

The covariate I am I trying to unstandardize is a proportion, so the values should be on a scale of 0-1
Below is a code I have been playing with. It runs without any errors, but nothing shows up in the plot. Perhaps there is something wrong with one of my values.
I'm also not completely sure the code is unstandardizing the values correctly.

UN.orig<- seq(min(covars$closed.P), max(covars$closed.P), 0.01)  ##covariates are in the original scale
UN.pred<- (UN.orig-mean(covars$closed.P))/sd(covars$closed.P)
newdata1<- data.frame(closed.P=UN.pred, total.BA=mean(covars$total.BA), roughness=mean(covars$roughness)) ##
EN.UN <- predict(AICc.sbest, type="lambda", newdata=newdata1, appendData = TRUE)
UN <- EN.UN*sd(covars$closed.P)+mean(covars$closed.P)  ### unstandardize predictions
plot(UN.orig, EN.UN[,"Predicted"], xlab="Proportion of Forest", ylab="Predicted estimates",
     type="l", ylim = c(0,500), frame = F, lwd = 2)
matlines(UN.orig, EN.UN[,3:4], lty = 1, col = "grey", lwd = 1)


Any ideas? Any advice is very welcome, thank you!

messages.author: 081fe993f0392c18
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Help plotting original values, unstandardize predictions
parts:
Hi Chitchat, 

You shouldn't unstandardize the predictions. The predictions should already be on the real scale when you use the predict function.  And the transformation you are concerned with is the one you did to the covariate closed.P.  You simply need to plot the output from predict() against the unstandardized covariates.

In other words, the code "unstandardizing" the predictions and plotting those results is unnecessary:
UN <- EN.UN*sd(covars$closed.P)+mean(covars$closed.P)  ### unstandardize predictions
matlines(UN.orig, EN.UN[,3:4], lty = 1, col = "grey", lwd = 1)
As you've already plotted your predictions on the real scale against the real scale of the covariates with this code:

plot(UN.orig, EN.UN[,"Predicted"], xlab="Proportion of Forest", ylab="Predicted estimates",
     type="l", ylim = c(0,500), frame = F, lwd = 2)

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Help plotting original values, unstandardize predictions
parts:
Hi Chitchat,

I think this warning is a bug related to changes recently made to unmarked to deal with situations where factor levels in the newdata did not match factor levels in the original data. You have two factors (site and transect) in your original siteCovs which you do not actually end up using in your model for lambda (which is fine). However in running the prediction unmarked looks for those variables in the newdata anyway to see if the factor levels match, finds that site and transect are missing entirely, and declares them "not factors" as a result.

After running some quick tests it looks to me like you can safely ignore these warnings for now, as they do not actually impact calculation of the correct prediction (assuming everything else is set up properly).

Ken

Here is the code in case it's needed.

#Plot influence of closed.P on response predicitions in the original scale

UN.CPorig<- seq(min(covars$closed.P),max(covars$closed.P), length.out = 100)     ##use datafile with original scale
UN.CPpred<- (UN.CPorig-mean(covars$closed.P))/sd(covars$closed.P)
CPnewdata<- data.frame(closed.P = UN.CPpred,total.BA = 0, roughness = 0)          ##use mean of standardized values for the other covariates in your model
UN.CP <- predict(AIC.sbest, type="lambda", newdata=CPnewdata, appendData = TRUE)
plot(UN.CPorig, UN.CP[,"Predicted"], xlab="Proportion of Forest", ylab="Predicted estimates",
     type="l", ylim = c(0,250), frame = F, lwd = 2)
